name: Whitechapel Gallery
known: Charles Aitken was the first director, 1901 to 1911 (Wikipedia).
The 2021-22 annual report showed a deficit of £73,016; the gallery restructured in 2023 and made six full-time staff redundant, three of them curators (USA Art News, 16 March 2023).
Whitechapel Gallery runs the Max Mara Art Prize for Women with Collezione Maramotti, the NEON Curatorial Award with NEON in Athens, and belongs to Allied Editions.

name: Zabludowicz Collection
known: Poju Zabludowicz is founder and trustee (Wikipedia).
Boycotted since 2014 over the founder's ties.

name: Auto Italia South East
known: Edward Gillman was director from 2019 to 2024.
Maggie Matić has been director since May 2024.

name: Barbican Art Gallery & The Curve
known: The City of London Corporation calls itself "the founder and principal funder of the Barbican Centre" (Barbican website).

name: Barbican Centre
known: Arts centre inside the Barbican Estate in the City of London, with a concert hall, theatre, art gallery, cinemas, library, conservatory, restaurants and conference halls (Wikipedia).
The Barbican site calls the City of London Corporation "the founder and principal funder of the Barbican Centre".

name: Belarus Free Theatre
known: The director Vladimir Shcherban joined in May 2005.
On 22 August 2007 police stormed a performance of Edward Bond's "Eleven Vests" in Minsk and arrested actors, directors and audience members (Wikipedia).
Companies House lists nine current directors: Michael Attenborough, Mark Ball, Baroness Helena Kennedy, David Lan, Jude Law, Dame Maria Miller, Alison Stanley, Laura Wade and Samuel West.
Khalezin, Kaliada and Shcherban are among the former directors.
Belarus.", a collateral event of the 61st Venice Biennale at the Church of San Giovanni Evangelista, 9 May to 22 November 2026, curated by Daniella Kaliada with Natalia Kaliada MBE (e-flux).
In March 2012 ArtsJournal quoted the company's founder warning that it faced closure in three months without significant funding and needed about 200,000 pounds a year to pay staff and cover costs.

name: Cubitt
known: Founded by artists in 1991 in King's Cross.
Wikipedia does not name the founders.
Runs 32 artist studios, a non-profit gallery, an 18-month Curatorial Fellowship (the Curatorial Bursary from 2001 to 2015), a Civic Fellowship and Cubitt Community Radio (Cubitt website;
Arts Council England: the website footer states it is "generously supported by Arts Council England", and Wikipedia says the Council funds the Curatorial Fellowship.

name: Francis Skaryna Belarusian Library and Museum
Hayward Gallery (Southbank Centre)
known: Joanna Drew was the founding director (Wikipedia).

name: Iniva (Institute of International Visual Arts)
known: Founded in 1994 to address "an imbalance in the way culturally diverse artists and curators were being represented" in the UK.
Stuart Hall was its first chair (Wikipedia, Chelsea College of Arts).
It was established in 1994 and renamed in 2007 in honour of Hall, Iniva's founding chair (Wikipedia).

name: Institute of Contemporary Arts (ICA)
known: It is a private limited company and registered charity (no. 236848) governed by a board of trustees chaired by Professor Dame Henrietta Moore.
Bengi Ünsal is director (ICA website).

A spokesperson said the ICA's deficit for fiscal year 2023/24 was expected to be around £800,000, and director Bengi Ünsal said "the pandemic, inflation and changing patterns in donations and grants" had led to an operating deficit for the last few years (The Art Newspaper, Kabir Jhala, 5 July 2024)
